title: Can you reach the Sun in one lifetime?
description: A traveller covers a thousand kilometres every day towards the Sun. The days needed are found by dividing the distance by the daily distance, then set beside the days in a hundred years. Keeko raises the doubt that a hundred years is so long that the Sun must be reached.
teaching_notes: One idea: days needed equal the distance divided by the distance in one day, and this is compared with the days in a lifetime. Watch for students who decide from the feeling that a hundred years is long, without comparing day counts.

source: Find out if you can reach the Sun in a lifetime, if you travel 1000 kilometres every day. (You had written down the distance between the Earth and the Sun in a previous exercise.)
video_script.why: The child can find a distance in stages and now divides a distance by the daily distance to count the days.
video_script.substitution: Days needed equal the distance divided by the distance in one day; compare with the days in a lifetime.
video_script.anchor: a traveller on a long road, the Sun far away, and the distance 14,70,00,000 km
video_script.wrong_answer: a hundred years is so long that the Sun is reached
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko decides from the feeling that a hundred years is long, without comparing the days needed with the days in a lifetime.
video_script.payoff_line: A lifetime of a hundred years is not enough to reach the Sun

final_answer.value: 1,47,000 days, about 402.7 years, so not in a lifetime
final_answer.spoken: one lakh forty seven thousand days, a little more than four hundred two years, so not in a lifetime

maths_rules: 36,500 < 1,47,000, so a lifetime is too short
the slip: a hundred years is long, so yes, with no comparison
video_script.design: One idea: days needed equals the distance divided by the daily distance, then compare with the days in a lifetime. The distance stays in the anchor; the working band builds each stage. Keeko's doubt: a hundred years is long enough.
